column1: # facts/sources.tsv -- the closed vocabulary of source names, and the artifact each one
# actually reduces to.  The design requires a guard to name two DIFFERENT
# sources.  Comparing the two strings for inequality does not establish that: `R6_decimal`
# and `R6_appendix` are two spellings of one lane, and a placeholder like
# The gate resolves both names through this table and rejects the row if they land on the
# same artifact.  A name that is not in this table is rejected outright, so a row cannot
# fabricatable  no   an artifact this repository's code cannot produce or alter: the real
#                    echovr.exe, a separate extraction of it, real captured wire bytes.
#               yes  a document, a summary, or a transcription.  A row may cite these, but
#                    tier V / V-PRIMARY additionally requires at least one `no`.
# supports     which KIND of claim this source can carry, so a runtime reading and a
#              decompile are not treated as interchangeable (S4.6 rule 4):
#                static   the artifact on disk or an extraction of it -- offsets, addresses,
#                         byte strings, sizes. What the build IS.
#                runtime  what the running system DID. Strong for behaviour; weak for
#                         structure, because a mapped image can be patched after load and
#                         a wire byte tells you what was sent, not where the field lives.
#                wire     what goes ON THE WIRE. Captured bytes are not weak corroboration
#                         of a message layout -- they ARE the layout, more directly than any
#                         decompile. A wire claim also accepts a `static` source, because the
#                         serialiser in the binary sees the same encoding; it does not accept
#                         `runtime` alone, since what a live struct holds is not what was sent.
#                both     a document. Weak either way; never satisfies the unfabricatable
#              A source may support more than one kind, comma-separated. The claim's kind
#              comes from the guard: G_CORPUS/G_WIRE are wire, G_HARNESS is runtime, and
#              The gate requires a row whose guard makes a STATIC claim to hold at least one
#              unfabricatable source that supports `static`. A harness observation may be its
#              SECOND source -- corroboration that the loaded image agrees with the file -- but
#              it cannot be the one that certifies an offset. That strengthens rule 4 rather
#              than widening it: the "at least one unfabricatable" requirement still holds, and
#              now the unfabricatable one has to match the kind of claim being made.
